label: Late original-phase h/0 (or y/f/r) after w/k/v/t were seen
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 3) & ((isin(in_tok, [tok("h"), tok("0")]) & (n_seen([tok("w"), tok("k"), tok("v"), tok("t")]) >= 1)) | (isin(in_tok, [tok("y"), tok("f"), tok("r")]) & (n_seen([tok("w"), tok("k"), tok("v"), tok("t")]) >= 2)))
explanation: Fires only in the original input phase at t >= 3 (never at t 0-2, the delimiter, or the copy phase). Rate peaks at original positions 5-7. The input token drives it: h is the main trigger (47% of activation mass, 12x lift), then 0 (23%), then y, f, r, with weaker contributions from 1, g, x. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of the token (92% of mass). History scales it: the rate and the largest activations go up when w, k, v or t appeared earlier, especially as the first token (first_tok w gives 4.7x lift). The top examples are all h or 0 in sequences that start with w/k/t. It does not fire on most other letters (i, l, b, j are near zero). The predicate is h/0 after at least one of w/k/v/t, or y/f/r after at least two. Precision is limited because the activation looks like a graded mix of the current token and the history, so a hard threshold cannot separate it cleanly. Dev F1 0.55, mass recall 0.73.
